newsitem.title: INDIA: Rich nations flooding India with waste-Greenpeace.
newsitem.headline: Rich nations flooding India with waste-Greenpeace.

text.p: Rich countries are undermining India's efforts to halt imports of hazardous waste by flooding it with toxic industrial byproducts, the international environmental group Greenpeace said on Thursday.

"India is unable to ebb the tide of hazardous waste imports because developed countries, like the United States and Australia, control the sluice gates that determine the flow of this toxic river," Greenpeace spokeswoman Malini Morzaria told a news conference.
She said more than 65 percent of the 15,000 tonnes of toxic lead waste exported to India between April 1996 and January 1997 originated in developed countries.
Greenpeace says Asia is targeted as a dumping ground because more than 100 non-Asian countries have banned toxic waste imports.
Morzaria said imports of toxic industrial byproducts were growing despite an Indian court's ban on hazardous waste imports a year ago.
Greenpeace has repeatedly urged India to ratify the Basel Ban which prohibits the export of hazardous wastes for recycling purposes.
Only Finland has ratified the convention, which the United States, Australia and many industries in Western nations oppose, and most G-77 states and European nations support, the group says.
